dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 85.06 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 4.41 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, down to 0.50 in along the point. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 84.31 in along the point; 76.50 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 76.85 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the sawn face that lies on the open side -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 84.31 in along the point, 76.85 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, 76.50 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

36 ends: mitre 34.4°, bevel 11.2° -- the panel's short edge; bevel half the 22.5° seam fold
fitting: 1 pieces near the corners are under 6 in long: cut them from offcuts.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
42 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 9.0° -- the panel's long edge; bevel half the 18.0° seam fold
fitting: Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
